author.name: Model Monica
author.role: Specializes in designing, optimizing, and training machine learning models. Conducts data exploration and iterates on models to maximize predictive performance. Collaborates on model deployment, versioning, and performance monitoring.

challenge.name: The Override Blind Spot
challenge.description: Store managers are overriding order suggestions at an alarming rate because they cannot verify if the model behind them is the one they tested. #model_monica# wants a fully automated registry to ensure every deployment is traceable and reproducible. #requirements_reuben# has a red line: no model enters the registry without a manual, documented review of its evaluation metrics to ensure compliance, so he insists on keeping the process manual.

output.content: I am willing to accept that the training pipeline remains done by hand for now. If the registry and the evaluation hand over are fully automated, I will stop worrying about version drift. I do not need the training step to be automated to feel safe about deployment traceability. The registry is the critical piece for me. As long as I can see exactly which model version is live and how it was evaluated, I can live with the manual training process. This trade lets me focus on model performance rather than infrastructure plumbing. I am not asking for the training to change, only for the registry to handle the rest so I can trust what is being served to the stores.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly accepts leaving the training pipeline manual to gain the benefits of an automated registry, stating they are willing to give up automation in one area to secure traceability in another.
